title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a hand-written plan on the back of an envelope, with items numbered ①–⑥. Items ⑤ and ⑥ are empty. It reads as an outline of different ways to give the data for a 'surgery' on a conformal (Riemann) surface. That fits the cote title 'Chirurgie des surfaces conformes'.

(1) A surface X together with a closed, oriented graph Γ drawn on it. Most likely this is a system of oriented closed curves or a ribbon-type graph along which one cuts and re-glues.

(2) A reference surface or 'type' X_0. A crossed-out phrase ('se donner ...') is replaced by a map j into what looks like an open set or tube, with a small sketch labelled X_0(ℂ). This is followed by '+ U_0 (or 𝕌_0) – données Γ'. The idea seems to be: fix a model X_0 and a local chart or collar U_0, then specify Γ relative to it.

(3) X_0 + 𝔞 ⊂ π_1(X_0) + Γ, with an arrow underneath that seems to say 'quotient/principal'. That is: specify a subgroup 𝔞 of the fundamental group. It determines a covering, in particular a principal (Galois) covering when 𝔞 is normal, possibly with the quotient group acting. The graph Γ is carried along.

(4) 'Torseurs Γ sur U, et Z ⊂_discret ℂ^*, Z ≅ ℤ.' Here Γ is reinterpreted as a group, and one considers Γ-torsors (principal coverings) over an open set U. The second datum is a discrete subgroup Z of ℂ^* isomorphic to ℤ, i.e. Z = q^ℤ with |q| ≠ 1.

The quotient ℂ^*/q^ℤ is the Tate/Hopf elliptic curve. Equivalently, ℂ^* (or a punctured disc or annulus) modulo a loxodromic generator gives a conformal torus. A q^ℤ-torsor over an annulus is the standard local model for gluing ('plumbing') two boundary collars with a complex parameter q.

So the page lists successively more 'principal-bundle' style descriptions of the gluing data for conformal surgery: graph on a surface, then model plus chart, then subgroup of π_1, then torsor plus discrete multiplicative parameter. This is essentially the standard way to parametrize gluings or degenerations of Riemann surfaces near nodes.
errors: No mathematical claims are asserted, so there is nothing to refute. The jottings are too elliptic to verify.

Minor point: a discrete subgroup of ℂ^* isomorphic to ℤ is generated by q with |q| ≠ 1 (or is a non-unitary loxodromic group). If |q| = 1 the subgroup is not discrete unless q is a root of unity, and then it is finite, not ℤ. So 'discret' implicitly excludes the unit circle; the note is consistent with this.

ideas.what: Specifying a conformal surgery by a closed oriented graph/curve system Γ on a Riemann surface X
ideas.modern_name: Cutting/gluing along multicurves; ribbon graphs / pants-type decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fenchel–Nielsen; Strebel/Penner/Harer for ribbon graphs; Grothendieck's own 'cartes' in Esquisse
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of maps/dessins and of the Teichmüller tower built by surgery on surfaces

ideas.what: Data X_0 + subgroup 𝔞 ⊂ π_1(X_0) determining a (principal) covering
ideas.modern_name: Galois correspondence for coverings / principal G-bundles
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Poincaré, Riemann); Grothendieck SGA1 for the algebraic version

ideas.what: Torsors over an open set U plus a discrete subgroup q^ℤ ⊂ ℂ^* as gluing parameter
ideas.modern_name: Plumbing construction / Tate curve ℂ^*/q^ℤ; complex gluing (twist+length) parameter
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (Tate curve); Fay, Kra, Earle–Marden, Wolpert (plumbing coordinates); Deligne–Mumford for the boundary of moduli
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (structure at infinity of the Teichmüller tower); not explicitly

deep.surprise_reason: This is a skeletal outline of standard ways to parametrize conformal gluing data: graphs, subgroups of π_1, torsors, and the multiplicative parameter q ∈ ℂ^*. It documents Grothendieck's 1983–84 interest in conformal surgery, which is already known from the Esquisse, but contains no new result or unusual connection.
transcription_corrections: Item ④ first word is most likely 'Torseurs' (torsors), not 'Trouvons': 'Torseurs Γ sur U, et Z ⊂_discret ℂ^*', with Z ≅ ℤ written below.

In item ②, 'trouvons Γ' is more plausibly 'données Γ'. The struck word at the start may be 'Courbe', replaced by 'type' or similar. The symbol read as ℍ looks more like a doubled U (𝕌 / U_0, an open set or collar), not the upper half-plane.
In item ③, the arrow beneath 𝔞 ⊂ π_1(X_0) is annotated with something like 'principal' or 'quotient', referring to the associated covering.
The sketch at the right of item ② is a small tube/collar labelled X_0(ℂ).
